title: Inverse product noise
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$ coordinates, let $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ be nonzero, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space. Applying product noise with rate $\rho^{-1}$ and then with rate $\rho$ recovers $f$: $T_\rho(T_{1/\rho}f)=f$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite product probability space $P$ with $n$ coordinates
A real-valued function $f$ on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\ne0$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $T_\rho(T_{1/\rho}f)=f$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
